question: Should OpenClaw add a per-target subagent concurrency contract, nested under `agents.list[].subagents`, that operates alongside the existing global subagent cap?
rationale: The need is valid, but choosing a new public config surface and defining whether global and target limits are hierarchical are product and compatibility decisions rather than mechanical bug repair.

options.title: Add nested target cap
options.body: Add `agents.list[].subagents.maxConcurrent` and require admission through both the existing global pool and a target-agent keyed cap.

options.title: Generalize named spawn lanes
options.body: Resolve this through a broader named-lane configuration and tool API, accepting substantially more configuration and scheduling surface.

options.title: Keep global limits only
options.body: Decline the new config surface and document process or gateway isolation for resource-constrained target agents.

recommendation.title: Add nested target cap
recommendation.body: Add `agents.list[].subagents.maxConcurrent` and require admission through both the existing global pool and a target-agent keyed cap.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history connects this person to the current concurrency resolver, command-lane model, and recent subagent policy work.
